title: Leave, holidays and time-off policies - 2025 handbook
summary: 2025 handbook rules for personal/sick leave, annual leave, pregnancy accommodations, holidays, unemployment, jury duty, funeral pay, military leave and FMLA.

claims.claim: Full-time active employees accrue Personal/Sick Leave at two hours per pay period worked, not to exceed six days per year, after 30 days of employment, with a stated maximum accrual of 60 days.
Absences must be covered by available leave and supervisor-approved to be excused; more than two consecutive workdays of Personal/Sick Leave requires a physician statement under this section.

evidence.note: Attendance section separately says a physician statement is required following three consecutive days of absence; preserve both statements for operational review.

claims.claim: Personal/Sick Leave cannot be transferred, is not used in overtime calculations, cannot extend annual vacation, and accrued sick/personal leave is not paid on termination or during notice of resignation.

Annual leave requires at least two weeks' advance request and manager approval; no more than two employees in the same department are to be on vacation simultaneously, and unused leave above the applicable limit is lost on the anniversary date.
Vacation schedule in the handbook: after 1 year, 5 days; 2-10 years, 10 days; 10 years or longer, 15 days; 15 years or longer, 20 days, with corresponding stated leave limits.

The handbook includes Kentucky Pregnant Workers Act guidance requiring a timely good-faith interactive process and describing reasonable accommodations such as breaks, modified equipment/seating/schedules, light duty, temporary transfer, time off to recover, and a private non-bathroom lactation space, absent undue hardship.

evidence.page_or_section: printed pages 17-18 - Kentucky Pregnant Worker's Act
evidence.note: Stored as handbook guidance; no independent legal-currentness determination is made.

claims.claim: Holiday pay eligibility begins after 30 days for regularly full-time employees in good standing with attendance who work the scheduled day before and after the holiday and work the holiday if requested; the handbook lists six paid holidays and eight hours of holiday pay.

After 30 days, full-time employees are eligible for jury-duty pay; the Executive Director must receive a copy of the summons before jury duty, regular wages are paid for time spent in jury duty, and jury compensation is reimbursed to RTEC.

After 30 days, full-time employees are eligible for up to three paid funeral-leave days for the listed immediate family relationships, with documentation and notice to the supervisor no later than the first day of absence.

Military leave for Reserve/National Guard annual duty is described as up to two weeks, generally not more than ten working days in a calendar year absent special circumstances, with written request to the Executive Director at least 30 days before commencement when applicable.
The FMLA section describes up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave in a 12-month period for listed family/medical reasons and up to 26 weeks of military caregiver leave in a single 12-month period.

evidence.note: Stored as RTEC handbook language, not independent legal advice.

claims.claim: RTEC requires accrued paid leave to be applied to FMLA and states FMLA runs concurrently with workers' compensation; a physician statement supports FMLA, employees pay their share of health/vision/dental premiums, and foreseeable leave requires 30 days' notice.

The FMLA section requires a fitness-for-duty statement to return and states that if an employee cannot return to the former position after 12 weeks, employment is terminated; the section also describes possible alternate-position placement if the employee cannot perform the former job and a position is available.

evidence.note: This is a direct record of handbook language; legal/compliance review is separate.

trigger: Employee need for paid/unpaid leave, jury service, bereavement, military duty, holiday eligibility, pregnancy accommodation, or FMLA-qualifying leave.
prerequisites: Supervisor/management notice and approval where required
steps: Apply paid leave, unpaid leave, benefit-premium and concurrency rules.
decisions: Whether an accommodation is effective and avoids undue hardship
Whether alternate position is available after FMLA where applicable
deadlines: Vacation request at least 2 weeks before leave begins.
Jury summons before jury service begins.
Funeral notice no later than first day of absence.
Military leave written request at least 30 days before planned commencement where applicable.
exceptions: Emergency absences may not allow advance notice.
Pregnancy accommodation is subject to undue-hardship language.
FMLA contains key-employee and eligibility exceptions stated in the handbook.

automation_candidates: FMLA document and premium reminder workflow.
